git_note: HEAD at run time; the stage-S2 code was uncommitted, so the code sha256s below identify it
method:
* Seed variance σ²_F at an endpoint = the across-seed variance (ddof = 1) of the family's
  per-seed video AUC (c40) or per-seed AUC_comp (T2).
* Test-set (cluster) variance: one joint source-cluster bootstrap of all six published
  models (``phase6_stats.hierarchical_bootstrap`` with each model as a one-seed arm, so
  every model sees the same cluster draw). From its covariance matrix, per family,
  v̄ = mean variance of one model's AUC, c̄ = mean covariance between two distinct
  models, d = v̄ − c̄ = ½·Var(AUC_i − AUC_j).
* Variance model (random effects): AUC_i(T) = μ + m_i + g(T) + e_i(T), with model
  effect m_i (Var σ²_m), a test-set effect g(T) shared by every model, and a model ×
  test-set interaction e_i(T) (Var d). The observed across-seed variance on the one fixed
  FF++ test set already contains the interaction: E[σ²_obs] = σ²_m + d.
* Floor (proposed decision, for user review at C1): since E[σ²_obs] ≥ d, the planning
  value is σ² = max(σ²_obs, d). A df = 2 estimate can fall below d by chance (Fair-N at
  c40 and on AUC_comp); the floor can only enlarge an MDE. Both floored (headline) and
  unfloored values are reported.
* A new arm = k = 3 new, distinct models of its family. For a contrast Σ w·arm with
  Σ w = 0 (T1, T2, T4, T5), g(T) cancels, so whether the test set is treated as fixed or
  random:
      SE_true² = Σw² · σ² / k.
  (The first build used Σw²·(σ² + d)/k, which counted d twice; verifier S2.2e F1, checked
  by a Monte Carlo test in src/tests/test_phase6_stats_mde.py.)
  The hierarchical bootstrap as specified (seeds drawn WITH replacement within arm, then
  one shared cluster draw) has expected spread
      SE_boot² = Σw² · (σ²·(k−1)/k² + d·(2k−1)/k²):
  the seed resample sees (k−1)/k of σ² (plug-in variance, which itself contains d), and the
  cluster resample adds d·(2k−1)/k² per arm because repeated seeds average fewer distinct
  models. In total it weights d by (3k−2)/k² = 7/9 against the true 3/9, so it is
  conservative unless σ²_m > 4d (σ² > 5d). Reported per test and α:
      MDE as specified (HEADLINE) = z_{1−α/2} · SE_boot + z_{0.8} · SE_true — the power
                          of the test that will actually run (its critical value comes
                          from the bootstrap; its estimate has spread SE_true);
      MDE true-variance (secondary) = (z_{1−α/2} + z_{0.8}) · SE_true — a test calibrated
                          to the true SE;
      actual α (as specified) = 2·(1 − Φ(z_{1−α/2} · SE_boot / SE_true)).
  The SE_boot formula is checked against a real hierarchical bootstrap of b7 ×3 vs
  Fair-N ×3 at c40 (both published).
* Retention (T3), R = (E2a − anchor)/(b7 − anchor) vs R = 1: by simulation. There is no
  anchor run yet, so the anchor gap G = b7 − anchor at c40 is a grid, plus two proxies from
  published single-seed c23-only ("lit") vs multi-quality ("mq") baseline pairs. For each G,
  (N̂, D̂) are drawn from their sampling distribution (Var N = Var D = 2σ²/k, corr ½;
  b7's σ² at c40, floor not binding), and the bootstrap of each simulated study is
  emulated by Gaussian draws with the SE_boot structure (corr ½); the test is the
  module's own: percentile p of R* − 1 with the +1 rule, and "not estimable" when D*'s
  95 % interval contains 0 (counted as no rejection). The MDE is 1 − R at the largest
  R < 1 with power ≥ 0.8 (the lower side). Headline = bootstrap-emulated (as specified);
  secondary = emulated spread equal to the true SE. Common random numbers across R.
